correctness.rationale: For the spheroid parametrization in RESULT.md 61–80, the meridional determinant divided by the dot product (one) gives tan(delta) = |r−1/r| sqrt(T(1−T)); the surface integral in x=cos(theta) gives total area 2πZ_r and the claimed density in T=x². Integrating on the two sublevel intervals produces the CDF; t=x² reduces the two primitives to integrals of 2 sqrt(r²+(1−r²)x²). Near zero, the equatorial branch starts at order u (H_r(t)=2r sqrt(t)+O_r(t^(3/2))) and the polar branch at order u² (w_r(1)=1). The endpoint identifies q and the scaled jet yields r=A_r/(2B_r); the informal 'their ratio' on line 86 means the ratio with the factor of 2 in the displayed formula. The r=1 atom is separate. At the upper endpoint, the symmetric integration interval has length sqrt(1−4u²); the odd density term cancels, and the angle change of variable gives 1−4u²=((4+q)/sqrt(q)) epsilon+O_r(epsilon²). For r→∞ dominate w_r/r by t^(−1/2); for r↓0 similarly dominate w_r. Normalization gives density limits (2/π)sqrt((1−t)/t) and 1 in L¹. The scaled complement converges locally uniformly in 0<t<1 to 1/sqrt(t(1−t)), which suffices with L¹ density convergence and no endpoint atoms. The two inverse branches of V=4t(1−t) yield 1/(π sqrt(v(1−v))) and 1/(2 sqrt(1−v)); their survival asymptotics after V↦2/sqrt(V) have the claimed constants and powers. Replay: RESULT.md 61–98 via these changes of variable. The supplied script is a finite recorded diagnostic, inspected but not run; it is not the proof.

value.rationale: An inversion-symmetric endpoint hides which axis is longer, while the equatorial and polar lower-end orders together recover that information after calibration. The contrasting beta laws predict genuinely different powers for rare angular deficits under opposite extreme-area limits. These are structural results for natural area sampling, not new numerical values of the classical patch formula. No statistical stability or uniformity across the limits is proved.
